correctness.rationale: For cyclic binary words, d_i=w_i XOR w_{i+1} has even parity. The (1,3) condition is equivalent to excluding transition triples 100 and 111, which forces nonzero d to decompose uniquely into cyclic runs 10 and 110. Marked-zero counting proves exact coefficients for all n and t, including small wrap-around n. The four-state weighted transfer determinant gives the bivariate rational series and zeta; Möbius inversion gives primitive classes and eigenvalue bounds yield growth. Replayed standalone brute counts 524286 binary words through n=18; independently checked difference constraints through n=14, matrix traces through n=70, and Newton sums through n=180. Finite tests corroborate an algebraic proof rather than serving as an infinite certificate.

value.rationale: The (1,3) class is the first nonrigid binary two-shift pseudoperiod with initial offset 1 following the rigid (1,2) case. The theorem classifies the entire natural periodic-point family by transition number and supplies all primitive rotation counts and the exact entropy. The cyclic even-parity renewal decomposition gives a structural explanation of the plastic-constant growth, not just a finite table or arbitrary numerical parameter. Scope is naturally complete for this fixed first positive-entropy case.
